import pandas as pd

# Load source tables
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_94/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_94/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_94/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source0 and Source1 on movie_id
join_0_1 = pd.merge(source0[['movie_id', 'title']], source1, on='movie_id', how='inner')

# Join the above result with Source2 on user_id
join_all = pd.merge(join_0_1, source2[['user_id', 'sex']], on='user_id', how='inner')

# Compute average ratings grouped by movie_id and title, filtered by sex
# For females
f_ratings = join_all[join_all['sex'] == 'F'].groupby(['movie_id', 'title'])['rating'].mean().reset_index(name='F')
# For males
m_ratings = join_all[join_all['sex'] == 'M'].groupby(['movie_id', 'title'])['rating'].mean().reset_index(name='M')

# Merge female and male averages on movie_id and title
target = pd.merge(f_ratings, m_ratings, on=['movie_id', 'title'], how='outer')

# Ensure columns are in the correct order and types
target = target[['movie_id', 'title', 'F', 'M']]
target['movie_id'] = target['movie_id'].astype(int)
target['title'] = target['title'].astype(str)
target['F'] = target['F'].astype(float)
target['M'] = target['M'].astype(float)

# Save the result
target.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_94/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read sources with index_col=0 as per hint 21
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_94/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_94/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_94/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_94_1 and Source3_94_2 on user_id
joined_1_2 = pd.merge(source1, source2, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Join Source3_94_0 and joined_1_2 on movie_id
joined_all = pd.merge(source0, joined_1_2, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Compute average rating filtered by sex='F' and sex='M' grouped by movie_id and title
def avg_rating_sex(df, sex):
    filtered = df[df['sex'] == sex]
    return filtered.groupby(['movie_id', 'title'])['rating'].mean()

avg_f = avg_rating_sex(joined_all, 'F')
avg_m = avg_rating_sex(joined_all, 'M')

# Combine results into one DataFrame
result = pd.DataFrame({
    'movie_id': avg_f.index.get_level_values('movie_id'),
    'title': avg_f.index.get_level_values('title'),
    'F': avg_f.values,
    'M': avg_m.reindex(avg_f.index).values  # align M to F index, may have NaNs
})

# Write output
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_94/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
